variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: GenAI monitoring is the continuous collection and interpretation of evidence about how a generative AI application behaves in production. It connects service health, model execution, cost, response quality, safety, and user outcomes so an operator can detect a problem, explain it, and choose a bounded response.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Monitor the complete user-visible path”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Service health
pairs.detail: Measure availability, typed errors, queue delay, rate limits, time to first output, end-to-end latency, and dependency saturation.
pairs.explanation: Measure availability, typed errors, queue delay, rate limits, time to first output, end-to-end latency, and dependency saturation.

pairs.label: Execution path
pairs.detail: Trace model calls, retrieval, reranking, policy checks, tool use, retries, fallbacks, and the versions that shaped the result.
pairs.explanation: Trace model calls, retrieval, reranking, policy checks, tool use, retries, fallbacks, and the versions that shaped the result.

pairs.label: Economics
pairs.detail: Attribute input, output, cached, and reasoning tokens plus provider charges to features, routes, tenants, and successful outcomes.
pairs.explanation: Attribute input, output, cached, and reasoning tokens plus provider charges to features, routes, tenants, and successful outcomes.

pairs.label: Response behavior
pairs.detail: Sample groundedness, task success, policy violations, refusals, citation support, evaluator disagreement, and human feedback by slice.
pairs.explanation: Sample groundedness, task success, policy violations, refusals, citation support, evaluator disagreement, and human feedback by slice.

pairs.label: Product outcome
pairs.detail: Track whether the user completed the task, retried, abandoned, escalated, corrected the answer, or accepted an unsafe recommendation.
pairs.explanation: Track whether the user completed the task, retried, abandoned, escalated, corrected the answer, or accepted an unsafe recommendation.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. An alert is useful only when it identifies the affected population, links to reproducible evidence, and names an owned action.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Service health: Measure availability, typed errors, queue delay, rate limits, time to first output, end-to-end latency, and dependency saturation. Execution path: Trace model calls, retrieval, reranking, policy checks, tool use, retries, fallbacks, and the versions that shaped the result. Economics: Attribute input, output, cached, and reasoning tokens plus provider charges to features, routes, tenants, and successful outcomes. Response behavior: Sample groundedness, task success, policy violations, refusals, citation support, evaluator disagreement, and human feedback by slice. Product outcome: Track whether the user completed the task, retried, abandoned, escalated, corrected the answer, or accepted an unsafe recommendation.

pairs.label: Name the boundary
pairs.detail: Define the quality floor, cost budget, latency objective, safety condition, or outcome rate before observing the result.
pairs.explanation: Define the quality floor, cost budget, latency objective, safety condition, or outcome rate before observing the result.

pairs.label: Measure persistence
pairs.detail: Require an appropriate sample count, time window, confidence bound, or repeated occurrence so one noisy point does not page the team.
pairs.explanation: Require an appropriate sample count, time window, confidence bound, or repeated occurrence so one noisy point does not page the team.

pairs.label: Attach the population

pairs.explanation: Include the affected feature, route, tenant class, language, risk tier, and exposure instead of reporting only a fleet average.

pairs.label: Link the evidence

pairs.explanation: Attach representative trace IDs, version changes, evaluator results, dependency status, and the last known-good comparison.

pairs.label: Declare the response

pairs.explanation: Name the owner, runbook, rollback target, exposure cap, escalation path, and condition that resolves the alert.

variants.prompt: Why is an HTTP success rate insufficient as the primary GenAI health signal?
options: A request can succeed technically while its answer, cost, latency, safety, or user outcome is unacceptable.
HTTP responses never include status codes for model requests.
Every successful request has exactly the same token cost.
Infrastructure metrics already contain the full prompt and response.
variants.explanation: Transport success covers only one layer; production health also depends on execution behavior and user-visible outcomes.

variants.prompt: Which alert carries enough evidence to be actionable?
options: A predeclared boundary plus window, affected slice, representative traces, owner, response, and resolution condition.
A red dashboard tile with no denominator.
A single evaluator score with no version or sample count.
An hourly spend total with no traffic or success context.

Add request IDs as a Prometheus metric label.

variants.prompt: A quality floor is breached, but the affected slice has sparse labels and the release has not been reproduced. What is the safest response?
options: Cap exposure and escalate evaluation rather than claiming a proven rollback cause.
Expand the rollout to gather traffic faster.
Delete the quality floor after seeing the result.
Average quality with lower cost and ship if the blended score improves.
variants.explanation: The breach matters, but weak coverage and attribution require bounded exposure and more evidence before a causal claim.

variants.prompt: Why should raw prompts, outputs, retrieved text, and tool arguments be opt-in telemetry?
options: They can contain personal, confidential, regulated, or security-sensitive data and need purpose, access, and retention controls.
They can never help reproduce a production failure.
OpenTelemetry forbids all string attributes.
Hashing always makes every identifier anonymous.
variants.explanation: Content can be diagnostically valuable, but collection must be minimized and protected according to the application's data obligations.
